The History of Lock Logic

From an old guessing game with numbers to a puzzle in which nothing is guessed.

Right place, wrong place

The idea of telling right digits at the right place from right digits at the wrong place comes from an old pencil-and-paper game, often called bulls and cows. One player thinks of a number with different digits, the other guesses and gets this answer after every try. The game may be a century old; around 1970 it became one of the first games on university computers.

A puzzle with fixed clues

Later the guessing game turned into a puzzle: all answers are given at once, and the code has to be worked out from them. Such lock puzzles with five clues spread widely on the internet in the 2010s and are now found in puzzle books and classrooms. Nobody owns the idea.

Lock Logic here

A player sent in the idea. PaperGames makes its own puzzles: a computer tries every possible code, keeps only puzzles with exactly one solution and drops every clue that is not needed.
